QC.Acc01.description: Is the source code managed with a Version Control System?
QC.Acc01.hint: The source code shall be managed with Git and remain publicly available for this criterion to be successful. Please check Pro Git docs about how to get started using Git tool. Guidelines provided by the most popular social coding platforms (GitHub, GitLab) are also a good starting point

evidence.message: Source code uses Git for version control

standard.title: A set of Common Software Quality Assurance Baseline Criteria for Research Projects

QC.Doc06.1.description: Is the software scope outlined in the code repository?
QC.Doc06.1.hint: A README file presents your software to the audience interested in your software project. Several online sites simplify the task of creating the README file, such as Make a README or readme.so sites. Be sure to add it to the code repository's root path

evidence.message: A README file is present in the code repository

standard.title: A set of Common Software Quality Assurance Baseline Criteria for Research Projects

QC.Doc06.3.description: Does the project establish a code of conduct for its participants?
QC.Doc06.3.hint: A CODE_OF_CONDUCT file sets the path for a constructive, respectful and positive atmosphere among all the contributors in your software project. Of course you can define your own, but in case you want to rely on external and widely-adopted code of conducts check out some of the most popular ones: Contributor Covenant or Citizen Code of Conduct

evidence.message: A CODE_OF_CONDUCT file is present in the code repository

standard.title: A set of Common Software Quality Assurance Baseline Criteria for Research Projects

QC.Doc06.2.description: Is there a clear path or guidelines on how to contribute to the code?
QC.Doc06.2.hint: A CONTRIBUTING file shall be present in the root path of the code repository describing the expected workflow to follow when adding contributions. Please check Mozilla's guidelines and GitHub's CONTRIBUTING.md example to get inspired on how to write a good CONTRIBUTING file

evidence.message: A CONTRIBUTING file is present in the code repository

.. option:: operation

   ``list filter``
      List the infrastructure IDs created by the user. The ``filter`` parameter is
      optional and is a regex that will be used to filter the list of infrastructures.
      This regex will be used with the RADL or TOSCA of the infrastructure.

   ``create inputfile async_flag``
      Create an infrastructure using RADL/TOSCA specified in the file with path
      ``inputfile``. The ``async_flag`` parameter is optional
      and is a flag to specify if the creation call will wait the resources
      to be created or return immediately the id of the infrastructure.

   ``destroy infId``
      Destroy the infrastructure with ID ``infId``.

   ``getinfo infId [radl_attribute]``
      Show the information about all the virtual machines associated to the
      infrastructure with ID ``infId``. Optional parameter ``radl_attribute`` to show
      only the value of the specified attribute in the RADL.

   ``getcontmsg infId``
      Show the contextualization message of the infrastructure with ID ``id``.

   ``getstate infId``
      Show the state of the infrastructure with ID ``id``.

   ``getoutputs <infId>``
      Show the outputs of infrastructure with ID ``infId`` (Only in case of TOSCA docs with REST API).

   ``getvminfo infId vmId [radl_attribute]``
      Show the information associated to the virtual machine with ID ``vmId``
      associated to the infrastructure with ID ``infId``. Optional parameter
      ``radl_attribute`` to show only the value of the specified attribute in the RADL.

   ``getvmcontmsg infId vmId``
      Show the contextualization message of the virtual machine with ID ``vmId``
      associated to the infrastructure with ID ``infId``.

   ``addresource infId radlfile ctxt_flag``
      Add to infrastructure with ID ``infId`` the resources specifies in the
      RADL file with path ``radlfile``. The ``ctxt_flag`` parameter is optional
      and is a flag to specify if the contextualization step will be launched
      just after the VM addition. If not specified the contextualization step
      will be launched.

   ``removeresource infId vmId ctxt_flag``
      Destroy the virtual machine with ID ``vmId`` in the infrastructure with
      ID ``infId``. The ``ctxt_flag`` parameter is optional
      and is a flag to specify if the contextualization step will be launched
      just after the VM addition. If not specified the contextualization step
      will be launched.

   ``start infId``
      Resume all the virtual machines associated to the infrastructure with ID
      ``infId``, stopped previously by the operation ``stop``.

   ``stop infId``
      Stop (but not remove) the virtual machines associated to the
      infrastructure with ID ``infId``.

   ``alter infId vmId radlfile``
      Modify the specification of the virtual machine with ID ``vmId``
      associated to the infrastructure with ID ``vmId``, using the RADL
      specification in file with path ``radlfile``.

      Reconfigure the infrastructure with ID ``infId`` and also update the
      configuration data specified in the optional ``radl_file``. The last  ``vm_list``
      parameter is optional and is a list integers specifying the IDs of the VMs to reconfigure.

configure lrms_front_end_lrms_server_conf (
@begin
---
- pre_tasks:
  - lineinfile: dest=/etc/hosts regexp='.*{{ item.1 }}.*$' line="{{ item.1 }} {{ vnode_prefix }}{{ item.0 + 1 }} {{ vnode_prefix }}{{ item.0 + 1 }}.localdomain" state=present
    name: Add nodes mapping in hosts file
    with_indexed_items: '{{ wn_ips }}'
  - name: Replace nodes mapping in hosts file
    replace: dest=/etc/hosts regexp='.*{{ vnode_prefix }}{{ item.0 + 1 }}.*$' replace="{{ item.1 }} {{ vnode_prefix }}{{ item.0 + 1 }} {{ vnode_prefix }}{{ item.0 + 1 }}.localdomain"
    with_indexed_items: '{{ wn_ips }}'
  - lineinfile: dest=/etc/hosts regexp='.*{{ front_end_ip }}.*$' line="{{ front_end_ip }} slurmserver slurmserver.localdomain" state=present
    name: Add master mapping in hosts file
  - name: Replace master mapping in hosts file
    replace: dest=/etc/hosts regexp='.*slurmserver.localdomain.*$' replace="{{ front_end_ip }} slurmserver slurmserver.localdomain"
  tasks:
  - block:
    - name: Add Master VPN IP in host
      replace:
        dest: /etc/hosts
        regexp: .*slurmserver.localdomain.*$
        replace: 192.168.255.1 slurmserver.localdomain slurmserver
    when: fe_hybrid_cluster
  - include_role:
      name: indigo-dc.nfs
    name: Call NFS role as Server
    vars:
      nfs_exports:
      - export: '{{ vnode_prefix }}*.localdomain(fsid=0,rw,async,no_root_squash,no_subtree_check,insecure)'
        path: /home
      nfs_mode: server
      nfs_only_v4: true
  - include_role:
      name: indigo-dc.slurm
    name: Call SLURM role as front

configure wn_node_lrms_wn_conf (
@begin
---
- pre_tasks:
  - lineinfile: dest=/etc/hosts regexp='.*slurmserver.localdomain.*$' line="{{ slurm_front_end_ip }} slurmserver slurmserver.localdomain" state=present
    name: Add private ip master mapping in hosts file
  tasks:
  - command: dhclient -v
    ignore_errors: true
    name: renew DHCP data
  - block:
    - name: Refresh setup data to get new ansible_tun0 item
      setup: null
    - delegate_facts: true
      delegate_to: '{{ slurm_front_end_ip }}'
      name: Add host VPN IP in master
      register: result1
      replace:
        dest: /etc/hosts
        regexp: .*{{ansible_hostname}}.localdomain.*$
        replace: '{{ansible_tun0.ipv4.address}} {{ansible_hostname}}.localdomain {{ansible_hostname}}'
    - delegate_facts: true
      delegate_to: '{{ slurm_front_end_ip }}'
      name: Add host VPN IP in master
      register: result2
      replace:
        dest: /etc/hosts
        regexp: ^ansible_default_ipv4.address.*$
        replace: '{{ansible_tun0.ipv4.address}} {{ansible_hostname}}.localdomain {{ansible_hostname}}'
    - block:
      - delegate_to: '{{ slurm_front_end_ip }}'
        name: NFS restart Debian
        service: name=nfs-kernel-server state=restarted
        when: ansible_os_family == "Debian"
      - delegate_to: '{{ slurm_front_end_ip }}'
        name: NFS restart RedHat
        service: name=nfs-server state=restarted
        when: ansible_os_family == "RedHat"
      when: result1 is changed or result2 is changed
    - name: Add Master VPN IP in host
      replace:
        dest: /etc/hosts
        regexp: .*slurmserver.localdomain.*$
        replace: 192.168.255.1 slurmserver.localdomain slurmserver
    - include_role:
        name: indigo-dc.nfs
      name: Call NFS role as client in hybrid
      vars:
        nfs_client_imports:
        - local: /home
          remote: /
          server_host: 192.168.255.1
        nfs_mode: client
        nfs_only_v4: true
    - include_role:
        name: indigo-dc.slurm
      name: Call SLURM role as WN
      vars:
        slurm_server_ip: 192.168.255.1
        slurm_type_of_node: wn
    when: wn_hybrid_cluster
  - block:
    - include_role:
        name: indigo-dc.nfs
      name: Call NFS role as client
      vars:
        nfs_client_imports:
        - local: /home
          remote: /
          server_host: '{{ slurm_front_end_ip }}'
        nfs_mode: client
        nfs_only_v4: true
    - include_role:
        name: indigo-dc.slurm
      name: Call SLURM role as WN
      vars:
        slurm_server_ip: '{{ slurm_front_end_ip }}'
        slurm_type_of_node: wn
    when: not wn_hybrid_cluster
  vars:
    slurm_front_end_ip: '{{ hostvars[groups[''lrms_server''][0]][''IM_NODE_PRIVATE_IP''] }}'
    slurm_public_front_end_ip: '{{ hostvars[groups[''lrms_server''][0]][''IM_NODE_PUBLIC_IP''] }}'
    wn_hybrid_cluster: false

@end
